notes: The mirror hosts, for tools/mirror_check.py and whatever fills them. A host is `ssh` (we have a shell there, so one walk of the tree answers everything) or `http` (we only have URLs, so the check asks for each file's headers). `holds` names the manifests that host is meant to carry, so a host can be for runtime downloads only. `base` is where a plan's URL for that host starts; a `%` in a file's own name has to be written `%25` there, because the server un-escapes a request path once (js/resolve.js mirrorURL). Nothing here uploads: it says what should be true, and the check says whether it is.

hosts.label: ovh1.p2pd.net
hosts.notes: Our own machine, and the only one that can serve a machine too old for modern TLS: plain http, no SNI needed (design.md 11.0 item 1). It also holds the build toolchain, which no installer downloads. Shared with soupchan, so nothing outside ~/installer-builder-mirror is ours to touch.

hosts.label: Cloudflare R2
hosts.notes: Planned second live mirror (2026-09-20): zero egress, about $20 a year for 120 GB, and Cloudflare's network is nearer to most users than one box in France. Not set up -- there is no bucket and the account is the operator's -- so `enabled` is false and `base` is empty; fill both in and the check covers it with no other change. Not a replacement for ovh1: Cloudflare's TLS needs SNI and a modern cipher suite, which Windows XP and Vista cannot do, and it does not serve plain http, so the oldest machines still need ovh1 (design.md, "Which mirror a plan should name first").
